title: Exports: CSV/Excel writers, list and dashboard exports
objective: Business users export filtered lists and dashboard tables to CSV/Excel with metadata headers, formula-injection guarding, and Internal-only cross-tenant export permission (spec FR-65, §16).
scope: Metadata block: tenant name, report date, data period, currency, last refreshed
Wire the Export buttons on Leads list, Parties list, dashboard card ⋮ menus, and the TopBar Export action
implementation_details: Infrastructure/Exports/CsvExportWriter.cs: RFC-4180 output; CsvInjectionGuard prefixes cells starting with = + - @ with a single quote; UTF-8 BOM for Excel compatibility; Infrastructure/Exports/ExcelExportWriter.cs: ClosedXML workbook with a metadata header block (tenant, generated at, period, currency, filters echo) above the data table, frozen header row, right-aligned numeric columns with full-amount formatting

Features/Exports: ExportLeadsQuery/ExportPartiesQuery reusing the corresponding List queries' filter contracts (same breadth permission); ExportDrillQuery{widgetKey, filter, format} for dashboard tables; format csv|xlsx via content negotiation param; endpoints stream FileResult with descriptive filename '{tenant}-{entity}-{yyyyMMdd}.{ext}'

Cross-tenant exports (any export executed under cross-tenant context) require PermissionCatalog.Global.CrossTenantExport (FR-65); normal exports require the entity's export permission (leads.export etc.)
UI: ExportMenu component (CSV / Excel) attached to DataTable toolbars and ChartCard ⋮ menus; TopBar Export button exports the current page's primary table when one exists; download via blob link
Exports audited (audit_log action 'export' with entity + filter summary)

e2e: exports.spec.ts: export filtered leads list to CSV downloads a file containing only filtered rows; dashboard card menu exports its table; Excel export opens with metadata header

findings.message: CsvInjectionGuard placed in QuoteIQ.Domain/Exports (not Infrastructure/Exports as the task files list stated). Rationale: the required unit test lives in QuoteIQ.Domain.Tests, which references Domain only, and the guard is a pure no-collaborator algorithm — matching spec §9.6 (isolated formulas in Domain/Application) and §17 (unit tests only for pure algorithms). The writers (Infrastructure) consume it via a Domain reference. Not silently resolved — flagged per CLAUDE.md.

Global.CrossTenantExport did NOT exist in PermissionCatalog. Added it (code 'global.cross_tenant_export') per FR-65 ('cross-tenant exports restricted to Internal users with explicit permission') and the task brief. Mirrored to the client permission list in TWO places the codebase requires: src/ui/src/features/userManager/permissionCatalog.ts (enforced by the PermissionCatalogDriftGuardTests) and src/ui/src/auth/permissions.ts (LeadsExport/PartiesExport screen-gating constants added alongside).

Excel injection mitigation: text cells (metadata values, headers, text columns) are (a) formula-injection guarded with a leading single quote and (b) assigned to the cell as a string — ClosedXML never stores a string as a formula element (only FormulaA1 does), and it consumes the guard's leading apostrophe into the xlsx quotePrefix text marker (Style.IncludeQuotePrefix=true), the OWASP-recommended xlsx mitigation. Asserted in ExcelExportWriterTests (DataType=Text, HasFormula=false, IncludeQuotePrefix=true). Numeric/date cells are written as typed values, never guarded, so negative numbers stay numeric.

No standalone /exports/quotes tenant-wide list endpoint was built. Quotes are lead-subordinate with no top-level Quotes list/nav (FR-45), and no tenant-wide quote list query exists to reuse. FR-65's 'detailed lead/quote lists behind summaries exportable' is served by the dashboard drill export (/exports/dashboard, ExportDrillQuery{widgetKey,filter,format}) rather than an unbacked quote-list feature. Endpoints delivered: /exports/leads, /exports/parties, /exports/dashboard. Flagged for the Evaluator/Orchestrator to confirm this reading.

Dashboard export (/exports/dashboard) is gated on PermissionCatalog.Leads.Export because every current drill widget returns lead-level rows (same rows the on-screen drill returns). Leads/Parties list exports are gated on leads.export / parties.export respectively. The cross-tenant export gate (global.cross_tenant_export) is enforced inside the handlers (ExportService.AuthorizeAsync) because it depends on ITenantContext.IsCrossTenant, which RequirePermission cannot observe.

TopBar 'current page's primary table' ambiguity resolved via a lightweight ExportTargetContext (src/ui/src/features/exports/ExportTargetContext.tsx): a page with a primary exportable table registers its export (Leads list, Parties list do) via useRegisterExportTarget; the TopBar Export action renders only while a target is registered, so pages without a table (forms, etc.) simply show no TopBar Export action. Flagged as the concrete resolution of that ambiguity.

Frontend lint baseline: `npm run lint` reports 1 pre-existing ERROR in src/ui/src/features/tenantManager/TenantFormPage.tsx ('_removed' unused) — NOT a file this task touched. New warnings introduced are react-refresh 'only-export-components' warnings in ExportTargetContext.tsx and Toast.tsx (useOptionalToast), consistent with the existing Toast.tsx provider+hooks colocation pattern already accepted in the codebase; warnings only, no new errors.

PASS. Independently verified against actual files (not the report). Gates re-run: BACKEND dotnet test QuoteIQ.slnx (real Testcontainers) — Domain.Tests 400 passed (incl. 14 CsvInjectionGuard + PermissionCatalogDriftGuard), Application.Tests 32 passed, Infrastructure.Tests 100 passed (incl. 9 export writer tests), Api.Tests 312 passed (incl. 6 export endpoint tests); 0 failed, no regression. FRONTEND (each separately): npm run typecheck GREEN; npm run build (tsc -b && vite build) GREEN (758 modules, no DashboardFiltersState field break); vitest 404 passed / 81 files. Stray-line hygiene: grep of all new files for <content>/</content> — NONE found. AC-064 fully satisfied; V-064 e2e deferred as describe.fixme with real bodies per established seed-dependency precedent (accepted).

CSV injection: CsvInjectionGuard prefixes ' on leading = + - @ plus leading tab(0x09)/CR(0x0D) per OWASP; null/empty -> empty. CsvExportWriter routes EVERY text cell, every metadata value AND the column-header row through Guard, then RFC-4180 quotes/escapes (" , CR LF), and prepends a UTF-8 BOM explicitly. Numbers/dates are typed culture-invariant values, never guarded (so a negative premium stays numeric). Unit + writer tests are non-tautological (safe-case coverage proves it does not blindly prefix). Effective.

Excel injection: ExcelExportWriter.SetTextCell guards the value AND assigns it as a string via cell.Value (ClosedXML only treats a value as a formula when set via FormulaA1), so a value like =cmd|'/c calc'!A1 can never land as an Excel formula. ExcelExportWriterTests asserts against that exact payload: DataType=Text, HasFormula=false, IncludeQuotePrefix=true. Mitigation is genuinely effective (defence-in-depth: text type + quote-prefix).

Permission/isolation/audit: entity gates leads.export/parties.export enforced at endpoint via RequirePermission; Global.CrossTenantExport enforced inside ExportService.AuthorizeAsync (depends on ITenantContext.IsCrossTenant which RequirePermission cannot see). Both 403-without (CrossTenantExport_WithoutGlobalPermission) and 200-with (CrossTenantExport_WithGlobalPermission) integration tests exist and prove the gate; Export_WithoutExportPermission_ShouldReturn403 proves the entity gate. Breadth honored: ExportLeadsQueryHandler/ExportDrillQueryHandler resolve leads.view_all and pass callerHasViewAll into the SAME list/drill filter contract, and ExportLeads_ShouldReflectActiveFiltersAndBreadthPermission proves a viewer without view_all exports only its one assigned lead, not the sibling — no breadth leak. Tenant isolation via ambient ITenantContext/EF global filter on the reused stores. Audit: RenderAndAuditAsync writes action 'export' with entity + filter summary; Export_ShouldWriteAuditRow asserts the row (actor, entityId, filters). PermissionCatalogDriftGuardTests genuinely reads permissionCatalog.ts and fails on any add/remove drift; catalog change is additive (no seeded-role/existing-permission regression; full Domain.Tests green).

FLAG-1 ACCEPT (non-blocking). Placing the pure, collaborator-free CsvInjectionGuard in Domain (unit-tested by Domain.Tests) rather than the task's literal Infrastructure path matches spec §9.6/§17 (unit tests only for pure algorithms). Writers consume it via a Domain reference. Sound.

FLAG-2 ACCEPT (non-blocking). FR-65 mandates an explicit cross-tenant export permission; it did not exist, so adding Global.CrossTenantExport (global.cross_tenant_export) was required, not scope creep. Mirrored to userManager/permissionCatalog.ts (drift-guarded) and screen constants added to auth/permissions.ts. Correct.
FLAG-3 ACCEPT (non-blocking). Excel mitigation verified real and asserted (see EVAL-SEC-2).

FLAG-4 ACCEPT as non-blocking, but flagged for orchestrator/human confirmation. Ruling: the pass bar for this task is AC-064, which requires filters preserved, metadata header, 'detailed lists behind summaries exportable', and the cross-tenant restriction — ALL satisfied without a standalone /exports/quotes. FR-45/AC-044 establish quotes are lead-subordinate with no tenant-wide Quotes list/nav, so there is no list query to reuse; FR-65's 'detailed lead/quote lists behind summaries exportable' is served by /exports/dashboard (ExportDrillQuery). NOTE the residual tension: spec §16's API table (line 481) literally lists '/exports/leads|parties|quotes' and the task scope repeats 'quotes', so if the product owner specifically intended a quote-level export (quote columns: version/valid-until/bound premium across leads), that is a follow-up capability (candidate for T-040 reports or a new task). Defensible interpretation; not blocking iteration 1.

FLAG-5 ACCEPT (non-blocking). Every current drill widget returns lead-level rows (same rows the on-screen drill returns), so gating /exports/dashboard on leads.export is consistent with what is being exported. Revisit only if a future widget exports non-lead rows (e.g. broker/RM-level) — then a widget-specific export permission would be warranted.

FLAG-6 ACCEPT (non-blocking). ExportTargetContext register/consume pattern is a clean resolution of the TopBar 'primary table' ambiguity; the target is registered only when the page has an exportable table AND the user holds the export permission (canExport gate verified in LeadsListPage/PartiesListPage), so the TopBar Export action never appears without both.

FLAG-7 ACCEPT (non-blocking). The single lint error is pre-existing in TenantFormPage.tsx (untouched by this task); new items are react-refresh warnings consistent with the accepted Toast provider+hooks pattern. Confirmed npm run typecheck AND npm run build are both green, which is the real gate.
